answer: One identity tends one island beacon. The agent stakes 80 credits, fits a pigment filter with a registered batch code to its lens, and files its flash pattern. An auditor recomputes the pattern from the tide-and-signal table; a missing flash or reused batch burns the stake. Fees rise for each beacon on the same funding key: first filing 30 credits, kth 30+8(k-1), 1000th 8022, so 1000 fake beacons cost 4,026,000 plus 80,000 staked. A rented-beacon ring fails: flashes carry one keeper's signature, so a reused batch burns both stakes. An honest keeper pays 30 once and recovers the stake.
